claim: Let G be a finite connected simple graph on n≥5 vertices and e edges. If G has no triangles or 4-cycles and diameter at most two, its ordinary cut complexes satisfy Δ₂(G) ↘ Δ₃(G). Consequently Δ₃(G) ≃ ∨^{e−n+1}S^{n−4}, interpreting an empty wedge as contractible; for the Petersen graph Δ₃(P) ≃ ∨⁶ S⁶.
integrity: The free codimension-one face of the Δ2 facet indexed by each nonedge is obtained by additionally omitting its unique common neighbor. The resulting elementary collapses leave exactly Δ3. The wedge corollary also follows from earlier Δ2 theory and is independently covered in a broader published Δ3 classification.
scientific_limitations: Requires finite simple connected graph, n≥5, triangle-free, C4-free, diameter≤2. The proof does not claim shellability, a classification outside this class, or independent priority for the separately known Δ3 sphere count. The numerical verifier is finite evidence, not proof of the universal statement.
title: A collapse from 2-cut to 3-cut complexes in unique-common-neighbor graphs
